objective: Define and enforce one Linux netdev/CAN-core ownership model for wbcan controller state across TX, bus-off, restart, link lifecycle, debugfs observation, and concurrent fault reconfiguration.
acceptance: the private fault lock no longer acts as an incomplete controller-state lock
TX, bus-off, restart, open, stop, and debugfs observation follow a documented Linux netdev and CAN-core ownership model
link stop disables and drains the TX path before returning and publishes CAN_STATE_STOPPED before cancelling restart work
restart can only commit from CAN_STATE_BUS_OFF and cannot overwrite a newer stopped state
the restart-stop test observes an entered restart callback before stopping the link instead of relying on timer probability
the default-off restart delay control is bounded and restored after every probe
TX fails closed if invoked in bus-off, stopped, or sleeping state
terminal state snapshots never report an awake TX queue
the private spinlock is not held across CAN-core or netif calls
parallel TX, state reads, fault reconfiguration, bus-off, restart, and link cycling complete within bounded test limits
the seven existing fault modes retain their observable behavior
the work does not add a second controller state machine beside the CAN core
evidence: bounded concurrent state, queue, entered-restart, link-stop drain, link-cycle, and debugfs probe output
clean readable marker-delimited dmesg segment without lockdep, hung-task, refcount, or soft-lockup warnings
KCSAN or PREEMPT_RT coverage is reported only when the tested kernel enables it
stop_conditions: the CAN core API contract must change
a private controller state machine is required
firmware, interfaces, or physical CAN claims are required
the hosted runner cannot load, restart, or unload the module
